spans.s:
Śṛṅga in the Rigveda and later denotes the ‘horn’ of any sort of animal. Hence the ‘barb’ of the arrow is called its horn in the Atharvaveda.
Foot notes i. 140, 6; 163, 11; ii. 39, 3; iii. 8. 10, etc.
Av. ii. 32, 6; viii. 6, 14; ix. 4, 17, etc.
iv. 6, 5. Cf. Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 154.

Śṛṅga-vṛṣ is the name of a man in one hymn of the Rigveda. According to Ludwig, he is father of pṛdākusānu.
Foot notes viii. 17, 13.
Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 161.
Cf. Griffith, Hymns of the Rigveda, 2, 142, n.
